# Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement

## Problem statement

The repository contains only documentation (`docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, worklog tooling) — no game code exists yet. The operator wants the first gym scene: a self-contained Phaser scene with only the player ship and space-style thrust movement (Asteroids-like physics with momentum and inertia). This will establish the project scaffold and serve as a testbed for core gameplay mechanics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A Phaser/TypeScript project is bootstrapped (package.json, TypeScript config, build tooling) with Phaser v3 as the game engine.
- [ ] AC2: A `Gym.ts` scene contains only the player ship — no enemies, no bullets, no HUD, no power-ups.
- [ ] AC3: Player ship responds to W/A/S/D and arrow keys with thrust-based movement: pressing a direction fires thrusters accelerating the ship in that direction; velocity persists and decays only via opposite thrust or slight damping.
- [ ] AC4: The movement model feels natural (not sluggish) — ship drifts with momentum, and the player must anticipate direction changes (Asteroids-style).
- [ ] AC5: Ship is confined to screen bounds.
- [ ] AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
- [ ] AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
data.title: Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement

data.description:
# Bootstrap Phaser + TypeScript project scaffold

## Problem statement

The AI_Hell repository currently contains only documentation (`docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`) and worklog tooling — no game code, no `package.json`, no build system. Every subsequent implementation item (starting with the gym scene) needs a runnable Phaser v3 + TypeScript project as its foundation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A `package.json` exists with `phaser` v3 as the game engine dependency and `typescript` as the language, plus `npm run dev` / `npm run build` scripts (Vite recommended, matching the GDD §6.3 web distribution model).
- [ ] AC2 — TypeScript configuration and a Vite/HTML entry point exist so `npm run dev` launches a browser window rendering a Phaser game; `npm run build` produces a deployable bundle.
- [ ] AC3 — The source tree follows the GDD §6.4 module layout (`src/core/Game.ts` boot/entry point, `src/entities/`, etc.) at least for the bootstrapped parts.
- [ ] AC4 — A minimal runnable Phaser scene (e.g., blank `BootScene` or empty `MainScene`) verifies the framework initializes (canvas renders, game loop ticks) — no gameplay mechanics yet.
- [ ] AC5 — A test runner is configured (e.g., Vitest) with at least one trivial passing test to verify the harness works.
- [ ] AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the new scaffold (README gains a "Run the game" section with install/dev/build/test commands).
- [ ] AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
data.title: Bootstrap Phaser + TypeScript project scaffold
